Contributing to shinyglass

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Keeping the R and Python packages in step

The repository holds the R package and the Shiny for Python package in python/. They share the SCSS and JavaScript, and they aim to expose the same functions with the same argument names.

Two checks run in CI (the Python workflow):

  • Vendored assets. python/scripts/vendor_assets.py copies the shared SCSS and JavaScript into the Python package. CI re-runs it and fails if the committed copy is out of date.
  • API parity. tools/api_parity.py compares the exports in NAMESPACE with __all__ in python/src/shinyglass/__init__.py, then compares argument names for functions found on both sides. R’s inputId matches Python’s id, class matches class_, and ... matches *args or **kwargs. Python arguments that start with an underscore are ignored.

Run the parity check locally from the repository root:

python tools/api_parity.py

When you add or change an R export

  1. Draft the Python version:

    python tools/draft_python_wrapper.py glass_plot_surface_input

    This prints a function stub with the R argument names and simple defaults. It is only a starting point. Read the R function, write the body by hand, add type hints and a docstring, and export it from __init__.py.

  2. Add a test under python/tests/.

  3. Run python tools/api_parity.py and pytest in python/.

If a function or argument should exist on only one side, add it to tools/api-parity-allow.toml with a short reason. Examples are helpers for R only packages such as ggplot2, gt, DT, or shinyreact. The check also fails when an allow list entry is no longer needed, so remove entries once the missing side is added.
